grh_ba40f28feeb1cb51dae9.title: The Adventure of the Blarney Stone
paragraphs: After abrasive Jeffrey Hankin bets that he will kiss the Blarney Stone, partner Michael Corcoran lowers him headfirst over the castle wall and apparently loses his grip when Hankin's boots prove greased. Holmes rejects suspicion against the hotel boot cleaner and reconstructs the climb. Corcoran's love for Hankin's wife supplies the motive, while his failure to react naturally to the grease betrays the method: he smeared the boots only as he took hold of them, making the murder look like someone else's earlier sabotage. Holmes proposes checking for the absence of road dust in the grease; exposed, Corcoran leaps from the parapet to his death.
